newsitem.title: GERMANY: OECD - Overview on Bonn's adoption of jobs strategy.
newsitem.headline: OECD - Overview on Bonn's adoption of jobs strategy.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development on Tuesday published the following assessment of how far Germany had gone in implementing the OECD's strategy for creating and maintaining jobs.
1. INCREASE WAGE AND LABOUR COST FLEXIBILITY Job strategy proposal
* Encourage wage differentiation, greater plant-level bargaining and opening clauses
* Facilitate the employment of older workers and reduce incentives for early retirement.
Action taken
* Minimum wage in construction was declared binding
* Early retirement age to be increased; part-time work of older workers is subsidised
OECD Assessment/recommendation
* Wage bargains should incorporate greater flexibility

* Reform eligibility for invalidity pensions; consider further means to curb early retirement (stricter eligibility criteria, actuarial discounts for pension benefits) and avoid long transitional arrangements.
2. INCREASE WORKING-TIME FLEXIBILITY AND EASE EMPLOYMENT SECURITY PROVISIONS
Job strategy proposal
* Reform regulations underpins inflexible working practices
* Liberalise terms for renewing fixed-term contracts
* Facilitate part-time work
* Reform dismissal protection
Action taken
* Renewal period and admissable frequency of renewals (of fixed-term contracts) increased; scope for secondments extended (period extended, approval requirement reduced).
* More flexible work arrangements in the public sector; subsidies to part-time work for the elderly.
* Exemption from general dismissal law widened; social criteria for dismissals relaxed.
OECD assessment/recommendation
* Review effects of regulations
* Monitor employment effects and continue with reforms if necessary.
* Avoid further subsidisation of part-time work for the elderly.
* Monitor the effects on hiring and the costs of dismissals
3. REDUCE THE DISTORTIONS ARISING FROM UNEMPLOYMENT INSURANCE AND RELATED
BENEFITS Job strategy proposal
* Reduce the generosity of benefits
* Restrict the criteria for not accepting job offers, strengthen penalties, tighten controls
* Lower social security contribution rates.
* Simplify the personal tax system and lower marginal taxes
* Reduce the generosity of sickness benefits and strengthen incentives to avoid abuse.
Action taken
* Minimum ages for receiving unemployment benefits increased by three years; redundancy payments credited against unemployment benefits.
* Qualification no longer reason for rejecting job offers; definition of acceptable wage narrowed; controls tightened, internal auditing introduced of criteria.
* Spending curbed in the pension and health funds and in the federal labour office, but social security contribution rates increased; presentation of a pension reform plan by an expert commission.
* Taxation reform proposal
* Statutory sick pay lowered from 100 percent to 80 percent.
OECD assessment/recommendations
* Abolish the extended period of receiving unemployment benefits for the elderly; increase the gap between social assistance payments and the earnings of low-income families.
* Monitor the revised criteria for refusing job offers or taking up employment and narrow if necessary.
* Curb social spending; coonsider other measures to place the pension system on a sustainable base (retirement age, basic pendion, funding)
* Implement the proposed tax reform
* Maintain policy
4. ENHANCED ACTIVE LABOUR MARKET PROVISIONS
Job strategy proposal
* Exclude measures from the requalifying for unemployment benefits
* Target measures at at-risk groups
* Base employment subsidies on wages below market rates Action taken
* Training period will not re-establish eligibility for another entitlement period.
* Support schemes for training of unemployed extended; more flexible work contracts for formerly unemployed.
* Admissible wage base lowered. Special conditions for the new Laender will be phased out.
OECD assessment/recommendations
* Continue reform.
* Monitor effectiveness; monitor the efficiency of work-in contracts, in particular in relation to employment provision measures.
5. IMPROVE LABOUR FORCE SKILLS Job strategy proposal
* Preserve and restore the attractiveness of the dual vocational training system, clarify its relationship to higher education.
* Shorten higher education and focus it on more occupational-oriented studies.
Action taken
* Curricula for apprenticeships revised and new occupations introduced.
* No action (on higher education).
OECD assessment/recommendation
* Continue to revise vocational training schemes.
* Shorten higher education and make it more occupationally oriented.
6. ENHANCE CREATION AND DIFFUSION OF TECHNOLOGICAL KNOW-HOW
Job strategy proposal
* Foster venture capital markets and reduce regulatory barriers Action taken
* Laws tabled to liberalise financial markets, ease access of companies to equity capital and change corporate governance.
OECD assessment/recommendations
* Implement proposed legislation
7. Support an entrepreneurial climate
Job strategy proposal
* Facilitate the establishment of new enterprises
* Increase the knowledge of the new owners of enterprises in the new Laender.
* Reduce the overall tax burden
Action taken
* Accelerated depreciation allowance for newly-founded enterprises, wage subsidies for small new-founded firms.
* No major changes (on increase of Laender knowledge)
* Abolition of wealth tax; reduction of the inheritance tax; trading capital tax being introduced in the new Laender; tax reform proposal.
OECD assessment/recommendations
* Continue to examine regulatory impediments
* Support projects to diffuse knowledge.
* Implement proposed tax reductions and abolish tax expenditures
8. INCREASING PRODUCT MARKET COMPETITION
Job strategy proposal
* Planning approvals needs to be simplified
* Liberalise shop-closing hours
* Encourage competition in the network sectors
* Market test services by communities need to be more closely market-tested.
* Pursue privatisation
* Reduce subsidies
Action taken
* Approval procedures simplified
* Statutory shop opening hours extended
* Law tabled allowing competition in energy sector
* No major changes
* Telecom partly privatised.
* Subsidies benefiting construction increased and reduction of coal subsidies slowed.
OECD assessment/recommendations
* Monitor the effectiveness of the new regulations and continue reform if necessary
* Liberalise further statutory shop openinfg hours
* Implement the energy law proposal and monitor whether regulations to enforce the opening up of networks are sufficient.
* Abolish preferential VAT treatment of public utilities
* Step up privatisation
* Avoid new industrial subsidies; set up scheduled for reducing existing subsidies.
--Janet Northcote, Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
